task.title: Parse CSV text
task.statement:
Write a JavaScript function `parseCSV(text)` that parses CSV text into an array of records, where each record is an array of field strings.

Rules:
- Records are separated by line breaks: `\n` or `\r\n`. A `\r` outside quotes that is not followed by `\n` makes the input invalid.
- Fields are separated by `,`. Records may have different numbers of fields.
- A field may be enclosed in double quotes. Inside quotes, commas and line breaks (`\n`, `\r\n`, kept exactly as written) are part of the field, and two double quotes `""` stand for one literal double quote.
- A quoted field must start right at the beginning of the field and be followed by a comma, a line break or the end of input. Anything else after the closing quote is invalid. A double quote inside an unquoted field is invalid. An unterminated quote is invalid.
- Whitespace is never trimmed.
- An empty string yields `[]`. If the input ends with a line break outside quotes, that final line break does not start a new record (so `"a\n"` yields `[["a"]]` and `"\n"` yields `[[""]]`).
- Return `null` for invalid input or a non-string argument.
